title: Observation of Fluctuations in Tetrahedral Clusters of Tsai-Type Icosahedral Quasicrystals and Approximants by High-Resolution Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy
content: Quasicrystals have a unique structural order which is neither periodic nor random. Tsai-type icosahedral quasicrystal consists of atomic clusters (Tsai-type clusters) with four concentric shells arranged in a quasiperiodic manner (Fig.1). The crystalline approximants of the quasicrystal are considered to have the same atomic clusters arranged periodically. The Tsai-type cluster has a tetrahedral cluster at the center of the cluster, whose fluctuation is considered to influence physical properties such as specific heat [1]. In this study, we aim to observe the fluctuations of tetrahedral clusters in Tsai-type quasicrystals and their approximants using a series of high-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) images taken serially from the same region of the specimen.
